answer: Use an opal-sealed skill passport. A newcomer locks a $140 bond and registers one key, then earns twelve stamps over 40 days, one per client job. Each stamp needs the client signature plus one random peer re-running the work in violet ink on the public ledger. Ten stamps unlock paid work; one forged stamp burns the $140 bond and bans the key for 90 days. Stamps drift through a nebula of 200 archives, so hiding one means rewriting all of them. Forging 1,000 passports needs $140,000 plus 12,000 real jobs, about 3,000 hours. Like a watermarked passport, one bad page ruins the book.
